Dated this the 07th day of March 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.363/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alappuzha, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 10.08.2009.

According to the petitioner, on 10.08.2009 at about 10.30 a.m., while he was riding a motorcycle, a lorry bearing Reg.No. KL-8 G 826 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.37,95,000/-
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the 2025:KER:22604 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 to PW3 and documentary evidence of Exts.A1 to A20 and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.23,29,230/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
Rajesh

9. Heard Sri. Sreelal N. Warrier, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
P. Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point:
In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner 2025:KER:22604 as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as Software Programmer, earning Rs. 4000/- UAE Dhs per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.25,000/-.
According to the petitioner, he was working as a software programmer in UAE and getting a monthly income of 4,000/- UAE Dhs, prior to the accident.
Subsequently, he got a better option and therefore, as a formality to join the same, he had to come back to India and it was at the time, he met with the accident.
Ext.A12 is the job agreement in respect to his first job.
Ext.A11 is the contract of employment with respect to the subsequent job.
As per Ext.A11 the scale of pay offered was 9000/- UAE Dhs including basic pay and other allowances.

The learned counsel would argue that, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner had to take rest for a period of one year, and thereafter, as per Ext. A20, he had to go to take up a new job where the salary was only 5,000/- UAE Dhs.
Therefore, from Exts.A11 and A20 it can be seen that since the petitioner could not join the second job, there was a loss of 4000/- Dhs per month.
The tribunal has fixed the notional income of the petitioner taking his monthly salary of 4000/- UAE Dhs corresponding to Rs. 50,800/- at the rate of 12.7 Indian rupees per Dhs.
After deducting  towards personal and living expenses, approximately half of the 2025:KER:22604 amount was taken as his notional income.

Since, from Ext.A20 it is revealed that there was a reduction in the salary of the petitioner by about 4,000/- Dhs, I hold that, for awarding a just and reasonable compensation, half of the above reduction in salary can be added to the income he received as per Ext.A12, which will come to 6000/- UAE Dhs.
When 6000 UAE Dhs as on the date of the accident is converted to the Indian Rupee, it will come to Rs.76,200/-(6000x12.7).

Since it was the income he expected to receive from abroad, half of the same is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the notional income for the purpose of assessing the loss of disability is fixed at Rs.38,100/-(1/2 of Rs. 76200/-).

11. The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would argue that the income claimed by the petitioner is only 16,000/- and as such the notional cannot be fixed over and above what is claimed in the petition.

It was also argued that, at the time of the accident, the petitioner had no job, and as such, only a notional income can be taken for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.
12.
It is true that at the time of the accident the petitioner had no job.

However, it is to be noted that prior to the accident, he was employed in 2025:KER:22604 UAE getting a salary of 4000 Dhs and he returned to India only after getting a better option for joining a new job and the accident occurred in the meantime.

In a similar circumstance, a learned Single Judge of this Court in Jyothi Lakshmi A. v. Binoy Augusthy [2025 KHC 1501], held that due consideration can be given to the salary received from the post from which the victim was selected before he met with an accident.

sentences.text: The evidence of PW4 and Exhibit A14 certificate shows that the deceased was also working as an LIC agent and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
The evidence of PW2 and Exhibit A4 shows that the deceased was selected as system administrator in a private company and was offered a monthly salary of Rs.35,000/-.

The evidence of PW2 and Exhibit A4 would show that the appointment offered as per Exhibit A4 with effect from 03/04/2017 is a regular appointment subject to periodical revision of pay and other service conditions.

The Tribunal found that the claim petitioner has duly proved Exhibit A4 through PW2 and fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.35,000/- for the purpose of calculating the compensation towards loss of dependency.
I find no reason to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal in this regard."
In the above circumstances, I do not find any merit in the above argument advanced by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.

13. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
(i) Lacerated wound on the scalp 2x0.5x0.5 cm (ii) Lacerated wound on the back of left knee-irregular wound exposing the knee Joint 2025:KER:22604 (iii) Lacerated wound on the knee ankle (iv) Type III open compound fracture of the lower end of left tibia (v) Dislocation of left proximal tibiofibular joint (vi) Type II pelvic injury (vii) Deep lacerated wound over the left inguinal.
region extending into perimeum with active bleeding (viii) Common peroneal nerve contused (ix) Injury to the left EHL muscle belly x) Tibialis anterior tendon cut and retracted proximaly 14.
As per Exhibit X1, disability certificate the petitioner suffered 51% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 51%, as fixed by the Tribunal.

Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.3,00,000/- alone, at the rate of 25,000/- for a period of 12 months.
Since 2025:KER:22604 the notional income of the petitioner was re-
fixed at Rs. 76,200/-.

I hold that, towards 'loss of earning' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 9,14,400/- (76,200x 12 months).
17.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the towards 'Extra nourishment' the tribunal has awarded only Rs. 5,000/- which is on the lower side.
In this case the petitioner sustained very serious injuries and he was treated as an inpatient for 25 days.
The tribunal itself found that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, he had to take rest for 1 year.
In the above circumstances, the compensation awarded on the head 'Extra nourishment' is on the lower side, and hence it is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
He would also submit that the compensation awarded on the head Pain & Suffering Rs.1,00,000/- is on the lower side.
Ext.A13 series photographs, also shows the irregular shape of his left leg below knee, because of loss of flesh.

Considering the fact that he was a software programmer employed in UAE and because of the injuries he lost his employment for a period of 1 year, I hold that the compensation awarded on the head pain & suffering is on the lower side and it is enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-.
18.

No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and 2025:KER:22604 reasonable.
19.
Therefore, the petitioners/appellants
